text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination on its own — in many clinical and hospital settings it reflects who holds senior posts, and such panels often appoint women. Treat it as context, not as your argument.

Your stronger points are concrete: a PhD versus a master's, eight years actually running a lab section, and an announcement justifying the choice with the vague phrase "broad leadership experience" rather than specified criteria. Weakest for you: "leadership" is a legitimate priority for a head role, and his management course speaks to it.

The unanswered request matters most. Send a written follow-up asking for the scoring criteria and how each candidate rated. Note the panel composition only if the reasons turn out thin.
